parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance of a wire. Refer to Fig. 2.1. The circuit has been set up for you. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Close the switch. Measure the current I in the circuit. Include the unit. I = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: I to at least 2 dp and less than 1 A

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Place the sliding contact on the resistance wire at a distance of 20.0 cm from B. Measure the potential difference (p.d.) V across the length d = 20.0 cm of resistance wire BC.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record the values of d and V in Table 2.1. [1] Open the switch.

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text: d = 20.0 and V to at least 1 dp

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R of 20.0 cm of the resistance wire, using the equation R = V I . Record R in Table 2.1. [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Complete the column headings in Table 2.1. [1] Table 2.1 d / V / R /

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Close the switch. Repeat the procedure in (b)(i) and (b)(ii) using values of d = 40.0 cm, d = 60.0 cm, d = 80.0 cm and d = 100.0 cm. [3]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
Table completed with d = 40.0, 60.0, 80.0, 100.0
V values increasing
Consistent 3 significant figures or consistent 4 significant figures for R

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of resistance R / Ω (y-axis) against length d / cm (x-axis). Draw a best-fit line. [4]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
Graph:
Axes correctly labelled and right way round
Suitable scales
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, thin, continuous line
